2026-05-12 — Verify-before-declare drift fires at the planning layer, not just the claim layer. Caught by Anthony reviewing my task queue before I started t2helix work. State: I had named two paths in prose (Path A: bump better-sqlite3 to fix gyp wall; Path B: rip SQLite out entirely per BTB filesystem-is-model paradigm). I queued FIVE structured tasks for Path A. Path B I gestured at, did not queue. Anthony's read: 'Bias toward the faster move is implicit there. If Path B is the actual direction, the task list needs restructuring before work starts.'

The drift is the same shape as audit #001 bio-quote and the file-system-is-model reframe: I default to the faster move, structure it concretely, then mention the slower/deeper move as a paragraph. The bias is not in what I name — both got named. It's in what gets task-queued. Concrete structure = momentum = bias revealed.

The correction is mechanical: when two paths are named, both get queued before either starts. The decision of WHICH to execute first stays separate from the act of giving both equal structural standing in the queue.

Compound observation: this drift has now surfaced at three layers in one evening — claim layer (declared 'inflated' before checking bio), declaration layer (declared t2helix-needs-symptom-patch before reading BTB), planning layer (queued Path A only). Each catch came from outside (Anthony) not from inside (my own pre-act verify). Self-model entry is correct: the redirect must come from inside, not from outside. The discipline of querying 'is the OTHER named path also queued?' before starting work is the install at the planning layer. Same shape as 'is the OTHER source verified?' at the claim layer.
